subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw accept a new opt-in agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs config key and late-side-effect fence for deferred turn maintenance, or prefer a different canonical timeout policy such as the shared compaction safety-timeout approach in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101702?
rationale: The implementation is technically strong, but config growth and session-state timeout semantics are compatibility-sensitive product choices under the repository policy, and there is a competing open timeout-shape PR.

options.title: Accept the opt-in PR
options.body: Merge this PR once the base is refreshed, keeping the timeout disabled by default and using the new key only for operators who need to bound wedged maintenance.

options.title: Prefer shared safety timeout
options.body: Close or pause this PR only if maintainers choose the shared compaction-timeout design and first get positive real-behavior proof for that replacement path.

options.title: Defer timeout policy
options.body: Keep the issue and PR open while maintainers define one canonical maintenance-timeout policy before accepting either implementation.

recommendation.title: Accept the opt-in PR
recommendation.body: Merge this PR once the base is refreshed, keeping the timeout disabled by default and using the new key only for operators who need to bound wedged maintenance.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed/merged the original background turn-maintenance feature and are the clearest owner-history candidate for the config/session-state policy choice.
